Direct test with the 600-unit gap constraint fails: temporal reachability from 798 reaches only 2 nodes and never 131 (step_01), and an explicit path enumeration under max_wait=600 returns zero routes (step_16). This is not merely a delay-budget artifact — relaxing the constraint entirely (max_wait=null) still yields no reachability, again touching only 2 nodes (step_03), so the failure is one of event ordering, not of waiting time. Confounder controls: the window is not sparse or empty (1775 events over 1375 active nodes, step_02), and an undirected/static connection genuinely does exist — the 2-hop neighbourhood of 798 (step_04) links into a broader component (step_07) and 131's own 2-hop neighbourhood (step_06) supplies the chain 798->132->583->934->368->131, with every hop confirmed present and correctly oriented as a static directed edge (step_08 through step_12). That static path is precisely the trap: ignoring time it looks like a cascade. Splitting the window shows why it cannot carry influence — the terminal hop 368->131 already fires in the early half, before 23500 (step_15), whereas the initiating hop 798->132 and the following hop 132->583 have no events at all before 23500 (step_13, step_14) and therefore occur only later. The chain is effectively time-reversed: the influence would have to arrive at 131 before it left 798. Endpoint activity is also thin (798 has 2 events/2 partners, 131 has 4 events/4 partners, step_05), so neither popularity nor volume supports a cascade reading. Conclusion: connection without temporal ordering — absent.
